predecessors.name: Greek city-states (independent poleis)
predecessors.text: the Aetolian tribal communities between the Acheloos and Parnassus

successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: Aetolia proper, a Roman client from 189/188, dissolved with the other Greek leagues in 146 and grouped into the province of Macedonia

ledger.x: 367 (earliest suggested founding): the league 'received Aeolis from the Thebans' in 367; 'its founding date is uncertain, with suggestions ranging from 367 BC to later'; infobox 'Established: 4th century BC'.
338: the league gained 'Naupactus from Philip II of Macedon in 338 BC' (Aetolian League page); the Naupactus page: 'Philip II of Macedon gave it to the Aetolians' (undated).
c. 301: 'Took control of Parnassus, including Delphi, which it held for over a century'. The Delphians and Phocians are the generic Greek counterpart.
280: 'Took Heraclea in Trachis, gaining control of the Thermopylae pass'.
c. 250: border conflicts led to Acarnania 'being partitioned between Aetolia and Epirus in, c. 250 BC'. Cliopatria shows the gain only in 230. The Epirote share is in the epirus dossier.
240s (undated on the page, which lists them only as the peak league's members: 'Locris, Phocis, Doris, Malis, Dolopia, Achaia Phthiotis, Ainis, Oetaea'): the central Greek cantons join.

c. 233: 'the Aetolians seized Ambracia around 233 BC' (Epirus page), as the Aeacid monarchy collapsed. The Ambracia page says only that during the wars of 220-205 the city 'ultimately joined the latter confederacy'.
Spring 220 to 217: the Social War.
Spring 220 to 217: Aetolian raids on Achaea.
219: Philip 'conquered several cities, including Elaeus and Oeniadae' after losing time 'with a siege on the Gulf of Ambracia' (Ambracus).
217: the Peace of Naupactus, 'held in the city of Naupactus', on 'the principle that every side should maintain what it currently possessed'.
217: infobox 'Territorial changes: Triphylia and Phthiotis to Macedon, Psophis and Lasion to Achaea'.
217: the Peace of Naupactus, 'granting the principle that every side should maintain what it currently possessed' (Social War page): the raids end, no land changes hands in Achaea.
211 to 206: the Roman-Aetolian treaty of 211 (Rome kept 'captured slaves and other booty', Aetolia 'would receive control of any territory acquired') brings the league into the war.
211: 'Later that summer, Laevinus seized Zacynthus's main town, handing Oeniadae and Nasos to Aetolia.'
210: 'Rome enslaved the inhabitants of Anticyra, and Aetolia took possession of the town.'
209-208: Philip 'took Thronium, Tithronium, and Drymaea, gaining control of Epicnemidian Locris', and in 208 'took Opus after Attalus's forces were caught divided'.
206: 'Without Rome's consent, the Aetolians sued for a separate peace on terms Philip imposed.'
199 to June 197: the league joins Rome ('the Aetolian League from 199 BC'); 'the Aetolians... sided with Rome at Cynoscephalae'.
June 197: Cynoscephalae ('In June 197 BC, Flamininus marched north from Elateia').
192: the Aetolians seize Demetrias.
December 192: allied with Antiochus III, 'the Seleucids and their Aetolian allies launched a campaign against the Thessalian League'; 'In early March 191 BC, the Seleucids invaded Acarnania'.
191: Philip V takes Demetrias.
189: Nobilior 'negotiated peace with the Aetolians and the Cephallenians'; indemnity '200 talents, with a further 300 paid over six years' after Rhodian mediation.
189: 'Ambracia was captured and plundered by Marcus Fulvius Nobilior in 189 BC'; Rome declared it 'a free city'.
189 (infobox 188): 'Aetolia was reduced to a Roman client state and required, exceptionally, to minister to the power and empire of the Roman people'.
189: the cantons leave the reduced league.
146: after the Achaean War 'all leagues and other political entities were dissolved' and 'the Greek states were grouped into the Roman province of Macedonia'.

wars.name: Lamian War
wars.outcome: Macedonian victory; the Aetolians, allied 'in mid-September 323', were the only state not reduced.

wars.name: Gallic invasion of Greece
wars.outcome: The Gauls repulsed from Delphi and destroyed on the retreat; the league 'defended central Greece against the Gallic invasion' and was 'admitted to the Amphictyonic League' (278).

wars.name: Social War (220-217)
wars.outcome: 'Macedonian and Achaean victory'; Peace of Naupactus on possession as held; 'Triphylia and Phthiotis to Macedon, Psophis and Lasion to Achaea'.

wars.name: First Macedonian War (Aetolian phase)
wars.outcome: Stalemate: the Aetolians made a separate peace 'on terms Philip imposed' (206); the Peace of Phoenice followed (205).

wars.name: Second Macedonian War (Aetolian participation)
wars.outcome: 'Roman coalition victory'; Thessaly freed, the Aetolian claim to its cities refused (196).

wars.name: Roman-Seleucid (Aetolian) War
wars.outcome: 'Roman coalition victory' (192-188); Aetolia 'reduced to a Roman client state', Ambracia captured.

certainty.note: Tribal cantons without surveyed limits; the 284 polygon is a proxy.
A federation of cantons and cities whose eastern membership (Phocis, Locris, Malis, Dolopia, Phthiotis) is attested but undated on the pages; the Acarnanian partition line is approximate.
The client league's extent after the 189 settlement is inferred (Aetolia proper and Naupactus).
